utterances.text: In the lead-up to the war and the war years, did you know Vidoje Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know -- when did you know that he was in the VRS for the first time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard that before he arrived. However, I don't think that he was with our brigade. I think he was with the corps in Vlasenica or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall him being stationed in Bratunac in 1993 at some time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say you were in politics during the war. What was your party affiliation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I was with the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1992, were you a member of the Bratunac Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you work with Miroslav Deronjic in 1992, 1993?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I worked with him at the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time period?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were in a powerful position in 1992 and 1993, the same position you were in in 1995. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, that is frequently referred to as an important position. However, I believe that from the very beginning they exaggerated a lot about that post. Many people used the term "president of the municipality," whereas I in fact was president of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And prior to the war, the majority population in the Bratunac municipality and area was Muslim. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in July 1995, the only Muslims in the area were in the Srebrenica enclave. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you follow Mr. Deronjic's statements as he pled guilty in this case and talked about the ethnic cleansing that he and the Bratunac officials were involved in from 1993 onward?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I heard some parts. However, I can't say that I heard all of his testimony because that was during my working hours. I am a teacher and I have to teach school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I said this was an ethnic war where both sides wanted to have the majority of the population in control?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I would agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including yourself during 1992 and 1993. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: My own position was not such. However, that was the public opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go to 1995. Were you still in the SDS in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that in March of 1995 the president, Karadzic, the top member of the SDS, had ordered the army, the VRS, to make life impossible for the inhabitants of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of such an order. I never saw or received such an order from anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that this order included an order to restrict the flow of goods to that enclave to make the inhabitants of the enclave dependent on the goodwill of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I've already said that I never saw such an order nor did I participate nor could I have participated in such an action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in Bratunac during the time period of 1994 and the lead-up to July of 1995. Did you see the slow strangling of convoys into the enclave, what has been described by the DutchBat as convoy terror?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection to "the slow strangling of the convoys," and what the DutchBat may or may not have characterised it as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I guess you have no objections to the gist of this question, just for using some words?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. Other than that, he can ask what he observed. I don't have a problem, but to those inflammatory words, because I believe those are his words. That's not what we believe occurred. Yes, I do object just to the words but not to the question itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey, you might rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can pick another word, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But I can also use the words of Mr. Karadzic which will perhaps ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the humanitarian -- sorry. Can you hear all right now?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the humanitarian convoys to the enclave were slowly cut off and restricted at an ever-increasing rate?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I had no information as to who was sending the convoy, nor did I know how much was needed up there to distribute it to everyone. So I don't know why you are asking me this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know anything about any of the convoys that went into the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. That's a mischaracterisation to what the gentleman stated. He didn't say that he didn't know anything about convoys, but he objected to having any knowledge with respect to the previous question the way it was asked. So I would respectfully request for Mr. McCloskey to be very careful in not trying to put words into the witness's mouth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think at this stage the witness has the right to agree with the Prosecution or to object to any questions. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I totally agree, Your Honour. I totally agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But the Prosecution does not have the right to mischaracterise or twist and turn the witness's answer in the form of his following question. That's what I'm objecting to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But I'm not thinking in this way. I think the Prosecution is just leading the witness step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I beg to differ, but very well. I accept the Court's ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you know anything about the convoys that were going into the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: The convoys passed through Bratunac and I saw them passing through the town. Now, as to who was sending them, I knew nothing about that. I couldn't increase their speed or volume or decrease it or do anything about it. I had nothing to do with international humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as you know, the civilian -- through the civilian authority and the other civilian authorities had nothing to do with whether or not convoys went in or went out of the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Nobody informed us about that, nor did I consider that somebody had to inform us about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that the Dutch Battalion's materials and supplies and food were also being slowly cut off up until July 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I can reiterate what I've already stated. I didn't know what were the needs of the Srebrenica enclave. I didn't know how much aid they needed. I didn't know whether what was arriving there was sufficient or insufficient, and I don't see why should I have known this. The Dutch Battalion for a while was receiving supplies from Bratunac. Now, as to whether the Dutch Battalion was in some kind of a crisis or not, that's the first I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you spoke of different commanders of the Bratunac Brigade. Thought the years of the war, what were your basic contacts with the commanders of the Bratunac Brigade, just roughly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Officially?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Just official contacts. Through the Executive Board, we had to use the unit with the work obligation to provide food, cigarettes, medication for the population, take care of the handicapped persons, assist families, assist refugees who were pouring in from other municipalities which was frequent in view of the combat going on. Very often the municipality had to pay for the funerals, and our budget was very modest to begin with. So due to the work obligation, all of the companies barely managed to cover those expenses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was helping support the army and the war effort part of your job and the community's job?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: With respect to the goods that I've mentioned, just those goods; and with respect to all other matters, we were unable to help them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the army was pretty demanding in requesting the materials you've described, I take it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't have a choice. You needed to do what they told you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: We had to use the labour force that we had at our disposal to give the utmost under the circumstances and everything was used mostly to provide for the needs of the population and for the army, the ones that I've enumerated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many different commanders were there in the Bratunac Brigade from the beginning of the war in 1992 when the brigade was formed, in November of 1992, just roughly if you know?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: More than six, definitely more. I couldn't give you the exact figure, but there were at least six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember telling Mr. Ruez something like 12 or 13 when you were interviewed a long time ago by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. It seems to me that every few months there was a new commander. But I told you just now that I was sure that there were more than six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I've got an exhibit I'd like to mark because I want to just make a reference to it. It's P845. It is a document that was seized from the Bratunac Brigade entitled the: "War history of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade." I don't want to go through the details of that with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This has not been previously admitted. There's no foundation for this document, it was referenced in the Butler report. But the gentleman, who for instance generated this so-called history has never testified. There's nothing in the Butler report that he met with this gentleman who authored this. So I do object at this point in time in showing this particular witness a document which the Prosecution has not authenticated and laid a proper foundation to. We have seen the document. I am aware of the document. But if we're going to say that this document is true, accurate, and complete in what it has and then use this document as a basis of confronting this particular witness or refreshing's witness's memory or trying to get this witness to substantiate something in the document, I would have to object unless Mr. McCloskey can give us an offer of proof at this point in time as to how he intends to lay the foundation in order to get this document admitted, Your Honour. Very well, I think I made my position clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Frankly speaking, I think we had the same doubts as you did concerning the authenticity of this document, because we just received this document a few minutes before. I leafed through it. We don't know about the author, the source, anything about it. I am prepared to deal with the issue when we discuss about the admission of this document at a later stage. But at this stage, especially in the cross-examination, I believe that Mr. McCloskey is entitled to use this document to ask some questions to this witness depends on the answers given by this witness. Should we proceed on the basis of this document at this moment and later on we'll see whether we should admit it into the evidence or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. And I have no objections to proceeding as long as the record is rather clear that I do not waive any objections, and I would be able to even object and request that any answers given by this gentleman be disregarded on the record unless authentication can be established or we're sufficiently satisfied for the document to come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll deal with it at a later stage. We'll bear in mind your objections at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this document that was seized from the Bratunac Brigade, we don't need to -- we don't need to give him the document. I'm not asking him to look at it. It purports to be a history of the brigade and it lists the different commanders that took over at various times. And I just very simply and briefly want to mention the names of each of those commanders and tell me if you remember them being the commander. Maybe if you remember there's some other ones, too. It said: "The brigade was established on 14 November 1992, and the commander was Lieutenant Colonel Borivoje Tesic." Do you remember him at the beginning of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then 22 December, 1992, it says that "Tesic was replaced by a Lieutenant Colonel Milan Urosevic." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it says: "On 1 April 1993 that -- excuse me, it says that on 3 February 1993, a Lieutenant Colonel Slavko Ognjenovic replaced Urosevic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: He was the brigade commander -- yes, he was. I don't know who replaced him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, this says on 1 April 1993 Colonel Cvjetin Vuksic replaced Ognjenovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: He also was the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it says that on the 22nd of September, 1993, Lieutenant Colonel Slavko Ognjenovic was again made commander and replaced Vuksic. Do you remember that happening?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so then we go all the way through the fall of 1993 all the way through 1994. And then we have May of 1995 where it says that Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic replaced Ognjenovic and was there through the end of the war. Does that sound about right to you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I think he came after Ognjenovic. I don't know the chronology. I know the names that you've mentioned. I know that all of them were brigade commanders, but I don't know at which point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that Slavko Ognjenovic had issued orders and had a policy to make life impossible for the Muslims living in the enclave at Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: What he told the army and how he worked with the troops, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you know about his policy towards the inhabitants, the Muslims, of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a chance to look over your interview with Mr. Ruez that happened back in 1998 just recently?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I want to just ask you a couple of questions about some of your answers. On page 4, Mr. Ruez asked you on line 18: "Who were your contacts among the police for the Bratunac area?" And you say: "We didn't have any special contacts, since I myself being president of the Municipal Assembly had no responsibilities or jurisdictions over the police forces. They would receive their instructions and orders from the Ministry of Interior. And in the case of an armed attack or clashes, they would be put under the command of the military." Is that correct, that last part? "And in the case of armed attacks or clashes, the police would be put under the command of the military."

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Any time the brigade or the army in that area encountered problems, police, as far as I know, as far as I saw it, would also be used for certain military activities. Our police station and its unit, with respect to whom I had no responsibilities as I've said, that police was under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of the Interior. I was not in the position to issue any orders to them, request them to do anything, or to be accountable to me on any matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And a little farther down Mr. Ruez says: "And on the military side, what was the military unit in charge of providing the security for your town?" And you say: "It was the Bratunac Brigade." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, getting to -- closer towards July of 1995, were you at the handover of command for Mr. Blagojevic, Colonel Blagojevic, in -- when he became commander?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if I could show you what's been marked as P397. And I'll show you the -- provide you the B/C/S copy. This is a daily combat or a regular combat report from the Bratunac Brigade. And if you could take a brief look at it. We could put the English on the ELMO, perhaps. Is that you, Ljubo Simic, mentioned in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: That's how I'm called. I don't remember attending any handover or transition of duties between commanders. That has never been the practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this help refresh your recollection that the transfer of duties was carried out and that you were present along with General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I heard that a new commander was coming, that it was Blagojevic. And I heard that from the logistics officer who often came to see us about the supplies that we were supposed to provide. He told me that. He gave me some details about Blagojevic, and he told me that he would be a better man for the Bratunac Brigade than Ognjenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's get into July 1995. You mentioned that you had left the area right before the enclave fell. And do you recall telling Mr. Ruez that you had gotten approval to do that from General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I remember that. It's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was it that you had to get approval from an army commander?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't have to, but I did that out of courtesy. Because the general had come to the municipal building. I don't know whether he was on his way to Fakovici, his home village. I was going away for a while I said. I asked him if there were any problems. I asked briefly about his replacement. I didn't know if there were any underlying problems that caused his replacement. I didn't want to ask any further -- it's just that he happened to be there. He was a general after all. If he decided to grace me with his visit and to talk to me about our problems, I decided to take the opportunity and talk to him informally. I was under no obligation to tell him anything. I did so just because I decided to. I didn't have to say anything. Maybe you could say I had a big mouth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that when you returned you were told that you needed to go to a morning meeting at the Bratunac Brigade command. This would have been, according to your chronology, the day after Srebrenica fell. Is that correct, that you went to this morning meeting at the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since we know that the brigade -- that the enclave fell on the 11th, this morning meeting that you went to would have been on the 12th of July. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: If the previous statement is correct, then this one is correct, too. I told you already I had difficulty remembering dates, place names, et cetera, and I hope you will not hold it against me, that I did not learn these dates by rote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We won't worry about the dates then. I will just say this after the day Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I can easily orient myself according to events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us again who was at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: When I came into the office, General Mladic welcomed us. He was inside that conference room. I came inside with the president of the Executive Board. We were joined later, if I remember correctly, by Aleksandar Tesic, who was working at the Ministry of Defence. In fact, the municipal section for defence. I was expecting Deronjic to join us as well, but I remember very clearly that he did not come. He did not enter the office where meetings were held at the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why you weren't able to tell about this meeting to Mr. Ruez when he was asking you about meetings?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If I may object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the Prosecutor could point specifically in all fairness to the witness where Mr. Ruez asked him to describe the meetings so he would have been able to have that opportunity to respond to such a request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the Prosecution is asking an initial question just to try to refresh the memory of this witness. If the witness fails again, I believe that Mr. McCloskey will show the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well, Your Honour. But again the question says that Ruez -- when Ruez was asking him about meetings. So I just think that in fairness to the witness it might be good to point him to the right direction. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey, maybe you can be a little more specific in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't want to impeach the witness. I just want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand. Just to make things easier. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you tell Mr. Ruez about that meeting when you saw him many years ago?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I did tell him that there was a meeting and that I attended it. I can't quite understand your question in as far as you seem to be saying that I failed to mention something. I told him the same thing that I'm saying here today. Unfortunately I don't have this text before me to look it up, but to the best of my recollection I named the people who attended the meeting. I have no reason to conceal any details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's just -- maybe it will be easier. Maybe this will help refresh your recollection. Page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the gentleman could be shown a copy in his own language, Your Honour, and be pointed in the right direction, line, and page in his own language. I think that it's only fair since the Defence was required to do that of the Prosecution witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As you did before?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just show him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record could we know what exactly he's being shown, the page in the Serbian language I take it so we can follow it as well over here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have to be a little patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know, Your Honour. I'm just trying to assist as much as I'm able to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you could go to page 61 in your text and it's page 6 in the English text, lines 10 through 20. Mr. Ruez starts out and says: "According to information in our possession you were requested to participate in a meeting just at the nearby at the moment the enclave was falling. Do you have any recollection of that meeting?" And you say: "Yes, I was attending a meeting." And then you go on to talk about the meeting, and it's clear you're talking about the 10.00 a.m. meeting at the Hotel Fontana.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry that I don't have the audiotape. Now, it seems to me that the gentleman asked me also about another meeting that was held at a different time which I did not attend. And it took place at the Fontana Hotel or at the command. And I never mentioned that meeting to him. And I didn't mention it now. Actually, I'm not aware of it at all. All I know is what I said. In the morning around 8.00 a.m., I attended a meeting which involved talks that were more informal and did not resemble an official meeting; whereas, the official meeting took place at the Fontana Hotel at 10.00 in the morning, as I said. I remember very clearly that a couple of times the gentleman mentioned other meetings held at Fontana or elsewhere. And it was the first time that I heard from him that there was some two meetings at issue at the command or at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you -- I don't want to know about any meetings that you weren't at, so don't worry about those other questions. If you can take a look at your page 7, lines 16 through 18. In the English, it's lines 17 through 23. Mr. Ruez says: "And do you remember if this meeting was held in the morning or if it was held in the meeting?" This is the one at the Fontana that you have been talking about. And you say: "I believe it was held at about 10.00 a.m. I don't know about any other meeting was this was the only meeting I have attended since I have returned from my trip in the evening. I was informed of that that meeting was supposed to be held in the morning, and indeed I attended that one." All I was asking you is do you remember why you didn't tell Mr. Ruez about the one you're telling us about now.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I think ... Well, you see on the previous page there is a reference to that meeting. I really have to say that I don't understand what you want me to say now, what do you want to hear from me? I remember the gentleman asking me if a meeting had been held in the evening perhaps or at some other time, apart from the meetings I mentioned. And I replied that I don't know anything about any other meetings, apart the one that was held at 8.00 in the morning and the one after that at 10.00. I still believe to this day that it must be recorded in this transcript. I cannot go through it all now and find my way around it so quickly, because I saw it yesterday morning for the first time. I'm really sorry that I can't help you any further. Either I am failing to understand you or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No problem. I can guarantee you that there's no mention of that morning meeting, but let's not worry about that. Sometimes people don't remember all the meetings they were at. The fact was there was a meeting at the brigade command. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mladic gave you and the others with you orders to do certain things. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: He asked us for our opinion as to what was the best thing to do now. I thought he was sounding out what we thought was the best solution. He himself did not take any particular position at that time. He said that the residents of Srebrenica would be represented there and that that meeting would take the final decision. He also said that whatever solution is taken there will be accepted and all of us will have to work to implement it in the best possible way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that morning meeting, were you or anyone else issued any specific tasks by Mladic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I believe he talked about the options that he had heard about, the options that were in play according to his information. He said that we would be required to help out in our side of that job, food, water, and other supplies, the transfer of people who were ill or wounded, and who were at the time put up at the command of the UNPROFOR in that building that was already filled over its capacity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your understanding of Mr. -- the tasks Mr. Tesic received? Which one of those jobs was he supposed to be involved according to Mladic's tasks?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is getting ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am entitled to object because there has been no testimony that orders were issued to anyone. The gentleman indicated that this was a sounding opportunity for them to respond to Mr. Mladic's questions. And so the objection is that it assumes a fact not in evidence and this is so elementary that even a neophyte Prosecutor would be able to recognise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, if there's no order issued to Mr. Tesic, the witness can deny that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But the question, Your Honour, is suggesting that orders were issued. Had the gentleman indicated that orders were issued to us, I would totally agree with the Prosecutor that he could go forward and answer that question. But now he is suggesting that orders were issued. He can lay the predicate. There is no predicate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness answered in his previous answer. He said: "We would be required to help out in our side of that job." Which implies a sort of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when General Mladic issues you a task that he says is required, it's pretty much an order, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: It was an oral order, a verbal order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: You can take my word for it. That's how I saw it, as an order, and I had every intention of complying with it. I had very good reasons for it, even before I saw the situation with my own eyes after my absence and my efforts to cover it up. And finally, if I was asked to help people who needed help, I saw no reason to refuse. A refusal would be discourteous, to say the least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was your understanding of these orders that were issued by Mladic of Mr. Tesic's responsibility in relation to them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I do not remember what Tesic was told, if it was anything specific at all. But since he was in charge of mobilisation of the civilian defence force, there was no particular building where the civilian defence people were waiting to be issued with assignments. As the situation developed, they were asked or would be asked to participate in arrangements for supplying water or food, et cetera. I'm talking about my assumptions. I did not hear and I'm not claiming that I heard what Mladic said to Tesic about what he was supposed or required to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But Tesic was with the other civilian authorities when Mladic issued these orders?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I said that I think he was at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dragomir Vasic, chief of the Zvornik CSB, do you remember if he was at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the meeting at the brigade command or at the Fontana Hotel?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No, not as far as I remember. I saw him at the Fontana meeting for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then you went over and changed out of your army uniform and then went to the Hotel Fontana meeting at about 10.00. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. I left earlier in order to be at the Fontana meeting at 10.00, and I was there in time after changing my clothes. And I arrived at the time when I was due.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that meeting you described General Mladic as giving the Muslims several different options. Is that right? They could stay or they could go towards Kladanj or they could go to any place they wanted to go. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I think that the lady whose name I don't know voiced her opinion. There were also other people from Srebrenica who contributed something. I couldn't tell you exactly what they said. And after that conversation, General Mladic told them that he would go along with every option. He offered them both the option of evacuation and protection, not only to Kladanj or Tuzla as they asked, but also Serbia or Yugoslavia or maybe third countries. And he would also go along with the option that involved their staying there. That was what was said at the meeting. I think it can be verified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was General Mladic pretty amiable to the Muslim people at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: At one point he raised his voice and I was embarrassed. But he seemed irritated and provoked by the wrath of that lady, who had good reasons by the way because of the situation her people were in. And in response to that, General Mladic invoked the memory of the soldiers who fell in Sarajevo and elsewhere. Anyway, the situation calmed down after that and we stayed behind after the official meeting was over, in informal conversation. He left with two other men. That lady also left, and after that I didn't really see him again. And I didn't see the other two either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Ibro Nuhanovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I did not. I heard later that he was originally from Vlasenica. The president of the Executive Board who also attended the meeting told me that he was from Vlasenica and that he knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the last time Ibro Nuhanovic and his wife and one of their sons was seen was in Potocari at the 12th and 13th of July? They haven't been seen since?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. What is the relevance of this particular witness in light of what he is here to testify? There's no dispute that this gentleman is missing. There's no dispute and there never has been a dispute. But this gentleman here who's come here to testify is not here to verify who's missing and who's not missing. And I think it's unfair to this particular witness. And the question is merely designed to provoke and to embarrass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, we also fail to see the relevance of this question. Maybe you could ask more questions to give us some background on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can give you some relevance. This is the president of the municipality. He is at a very important meeting. The people that are representing the Muslims are also at this meeting. Those are the people that are his negotiating partners. And as Mr. Karnavas has said, it's very clear from historical record that one of his negotiating partners disappeared after that meeting. I think it's a historical part of this case, that is a simple question. And if he doesn't know anything about it, he can say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, from what I understand now, there seems to be a new twist to the Prosecution's case that somehow the negotiators were executed right after the meeting. That's what he's trying to suggest. If he can tie in how this gentleman here has any knowledge of what happened, I don't have a problem. I believe they have evidence that the gentleman chose to stay there and somehow was separated or somehow went missing with his entire family. We surely admit that this is a tragedy, but now to suggest somehow that the negotiators were targeted right after the meeting and killed to somehow lend credence that this was a preplanned genocidal plot, I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we don't think along your line, Mr. Karnavas. But, Mr. McCloskey, you may ask this witness whether he knows the whereabouts of this witness and his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And of course Mr. Karnavas's imagination has nothing to do with the Prosecution's position, as I'm sure the Court's aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about what happened to Mr. Nuhanovic and his family?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I said already that I expected him to join that team up there and that unfortunately I did not see him either up there or later. That's all I can say about him. That's all I know about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you one more question before the break about something that Mr. Mladic said -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm a little confused, Mr. President. I'll keep going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we have the transcript of -- as Mr. Karnavas told you some of this meeting was on videotape. And we do have a section of that videotape that I want to allow you to see and I wanted to ask you a couple of questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So if we could play that clip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember being there when he, General Mladic, made that comment?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see anything in that comment that might frighten the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe it was that Mladic was quite rough in his language. And I didn't like to be near him in these situations, because he was quite rough, cutting. I don't think that it was necessary in this situation. That could have been put in milder terms than it was. However, I couldn't stop him talking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your knowledge of the situation, did you find anything in that statement that would frighten the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, naturally this phrase "survive or disappear." It was not necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You earlier said that the Muslims were running to get on the bus, and that they even left their infirm relatives behind and you had to take them. Did it cross your mind that those people might have been getting on that bus because they were scared to death of what would happen to them if they stayed behind?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. They were probably afraid that not all of their requests would be met. They were afraid that there wouldn't be room for all of them in the transport in view of the experience they had in wintertime. I conclude this based on the sentence of the girl, student of mine, who asked me for help, asking that I use my power to ensure that the convoy would pass through and that all of them would leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says here: "There is no need for your people to get killed, your husband, your brothers, or your neighbours. All you have to do is say what you want, as I told this gentleman last night. You can either survive or disappear. For your survival, I demand that all your armed men, even those who committed crimes, and they did against our people, surrender their weapons to the VRS." So in this statement Mladic has conditioned the evacuation of the Muslims on whether or not all their men surrender, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I think that the gist of his sentence was that he urged Muslims not to put up any further resistance, because that could lead to further bloodshed and that would be ridiculous. This is why he urged them to surrender their weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't he condition the evacuation on the surrender of the Muslim men, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't see that this was conditioned. This was promised to them, so why would he condition it now saying that unless you do this there would be no evacuation? I think that their position was very clear. They asked for evacuation. And they could verify it with others upon their return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He goes on to say: "Upon surrendering the weapons, you may choose to stay in the territory or if you wish go wherever you want." That sounds like a condition to me. Don't you see it that way?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't see how would they interpret it had he said to them: "Stay with your weapons with you." What could they have concluded based on that? Would that mean they could defend themselves if somebody attacked them and that they would be safe there? Would that be the only possible interpretation?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, as you've mentioned, there was a Muslim army escaping through the woods, and they did not all surrender their weapons, did they?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I heard and that's what one could observe. I also saw that the only males there were the elderly, and then there were women and children. And it was the way you heard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those men that didn't surrender, who fought their way or walked their way through the woods, do you know how many of them disappeared, have never been seen from since? What information do you have about the number?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I heard about that, and I have said so today, that there was a lot of truth in it. And a further confirmation of that are the cemeteries that have been uncovered lately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I ask you if you had a number. Do you know roughly how many of those Muslim men do you believe disappeared, if you care to know or learn?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to that last part of the question: "If you care to know or learn." Now we're being flip with this witness. I don't think it's necessary, because the gentleman is not denying these facts. I think a little courtesy would be -- because this is my first witness, obviously this will have a chilling effect on all my other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think there is a reason for this objection. You may just drop off the last part. Or you may just ask, if you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can I ask him if he cares to know? I don't see the problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's too personal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn of any estimated number of Muslims that disappeared?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Did I learn?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I heard about the figure of 7.000 or perhaps more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that meeting, did General Mladic or any other authority say anything to the Muslims and Dutch about reviewing military age men to be screened as war criminals?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I did not understand your question. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mladic or any Serb authority tell the assembled group that the military age men in the crowd in Potocari would be screened to determine if there was war criminals among them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No, not military aged men. He said, and I think you could hear it yourself, that among the soldiers there could be something -- some people for whom there is evidence that they had committed war crimes. And I think that he said that such individuals would be detained and that proceedings would be instigated against them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you were in Potocari later that day, did you see military age Muslim men being separated from their families and detained?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No, nor did I have occasion for that. As I've told you, my scope of responsibilities was to deal with a tremendous number of civilians. And that's all I could deal with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So during that time period while you were handing out milk and juice and other things, did you see any suffering from the Muslims as a result of being hit or struck by Serb soldiers or police officers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No. The army and some soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade as well as soldiers from the Dutch Battalion tried to prevent the stampede of people who wanted to reach the vehicles. People were pushing back and forth, pushing each other. I could see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know there were soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: They wore uniforms of our army. No other army could have been present there. I have no information to the effect that there was some other army there, so I assumed that they were from our army, from our brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone shot or killed, any Muslims, around Potocari that day?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No. As I've said, I was told about a woman who had been wounded in the vicinity. I went there and I asked for medical assistance for her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports of any corpses in the area around Potocari, in the woods or anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I did not receive any such reports, nor would there be anyone who would be sending reports to me who would have such an obligation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the night of the 12th of July, did you receive any reports of rapes or murders or abductions from the Muslim population around Potocari?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: None of that. I heard nothing to that effect from anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge that at least 200 military age Muslim men were separated on the 12th of July and taken and stored in the buildings around the Vuk Karadzic school on the night of the 12th, that day after Srebrenica had fallen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: As I've said, I didn't see that. And I was not in the position to see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports that Muslim prisoners were being held in your town at the Vuk Karadzic school area?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall telling Mr. Ruez about the Vuk Karadzic school and prisoners being there at any time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No, I do not recall. I only said that I had seen buses in the evening upon my return with the people from the UNHCR. We saw buses lined up from the school onwards behind the municipal building. However, these buses were empty. And since it was already evening time, I took it to mean that the evacuation had been completed for that day and that it would continue the following one. So this didn't look strange to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the night of the 12th, that day after the fall of Srebrenica, did you receive any reports that Muslim men were being murdered in and around the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No. Nobody reported that to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, did you become aware that thousands of Muslims were being detained in and around the Vuk Karadzic school complex as well as in vehicles up and down the streets of Bratunac on the afternoon and evening of the 13th of July, two days after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: The vehicles that president of the Executive Board told me about I've already said everything that I had to say about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know anything else about the thousands of Muslims that were detained in Bratunac on the afternoon/evening of 13th July?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about the effort to pick up the dead bodies left over from that evening on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of any effort to pick up bodies of dead Muslims in the city of Bratunac on the 14th of July, after ...

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who may have told Dragan Mirkovic to arrange for the retrieval of many bodies from the town of Bratunac at about that date?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Somebody from the army. At least I was taught that in war operations the army usually has a unit involved in cleaning up of the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not aware of any combat that was going on in the Bratunac town on that night, are you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Colonel Blagojevic at the supply centre in Bratunac, can you tell us where that is in Bratunac, what's the address?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: This is the street leading up to Srebrenica. It's on the outskirts of the town, next to the main street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell what he was doing there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: He stood there with another man when I came by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in uniform?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the other man, if you know?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I didn't really look carefully. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly what time of day was this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: It was towards the evening. It could have been around 8.00, around that time. A little bit before, a little bit after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is at that site?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: It's a building of the distribution centre where the warehouse of the Red Cross was, because the commercial enterprise who normally owned this site didn't have any goods, wasn't functioning as it did before the war. So they lent this site to the Red Cross. So the Red Cross was storing its supplies there in order to distribute it to the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the Muslim men that were murdered at the Kravica warehouse were put?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Just for the clarity of the record. "Put," put before the incident? After the incident? I'm not quite clear, so I think there's some clarification that is needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness answered that he does not know, no matter in which situation. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any mass grave anywhere near Bratunac containing any bodies of Muslims from July 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't. Somebody in the army in charge of the cleaning up of the area must have been involved in this. And I doubt that that person would be revealing any of this information to me or to anyone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I told you there was a mass grave in Glogova that had more than a thousand bodies in it after these events of July 1995, would that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Probably due to the fact of how close this is to the place in Kravica where the events happened. This made it probably convenient for somebody in the army to bury these people in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Glogova was a Muslim village before the war, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the efforts to unbury these thousands -- over a thousand bodies from the Glogova grave and move them into scattered graves in the area?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you really think that the army would be telling such things to us?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Information provided that the trucks carrying corpses went through town and you could smell it for days and children were finding things on the streets and that everybody in the town knew about it. Were those just stories?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know that it was done during the day. It was possible that it was done during the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Colonel Beara at Miroslav Deronjic's office in the late-night hours of 13 July, a couple of days after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I did not. I've said that in the morning upon hearing the news from the president of the Executive Board, I went to him because he was a duty officer. And I asked that the buses with people at the stadium be evacuated from Bratunac, as had been agreed and done prior to that. I've said today that I did not know that man before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know of a soldier in the Red Beret unit named Miroslav Stanojevic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was killed a while back in an auto accident after the war sometime?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about any soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade being involved in the killings at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I just have one question, Mr. Witness. You said that on one occasion you talked with Mr. Blagojevic and Mladic outside the scope but still the period was still in July. When was that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I've said that I was bad with dates. It is true that the two of us were asked by General Mladic to go to Crna Rijeka and we attended that meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What was discussed during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I think that the meeting was completely pointless and useless. I didn't know until I got there - and neither did Colonel Blagojevic - why we were invited to attend. Later on it turned out that we were invited because somebody had told him that I was advocating the abolition of some military co-ops. He had probably heard what my position on the matter was. He had probably heard that I called them Sovhoz or Kolhoz or something like that. And based on that he probably concluded that I wished them to be disbanded. So because of that, president of the Executive Board and president of Kalesija municipality were also invited to attend. He yelled at them quite badly and also at me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions out of these questions? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just one clarification. Further examination by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was some military co-op and you gave the term of that, I believe. Is that correct? That's what it turned out to be?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And General Mladic thought there was an attempt to somehow disband these sort of co-ops and that's why he was a lashing out at some of the people. That was your understanding?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I think that he was under the impression or perhaps somebody told him that on purpose that I was supporting this, I was advocating this. And this is the reason why I was invited to attend. And I was told very harshly to not do that. General Zivanovic supported this as well. This had no economic justification from the very beginning. However, they operated somehow. And basically it was a bad investment. We invested more than we got out of it. And I was quite open in voicing this. I think that this is why they were angry at me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage, are there any documents to tender? I guess there's none from --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do have the war history document that does lay out the commanders of the various brigades, which is an issue that has been repeated by the Defence several times. It's from the same collection of all the rest of our documents and it was captured at the same time as the rest. And it's a well-known document to everyone, well on this side anyway, that we've been sharing this material for years. So I thought it may be of some help to the Court to see what it said about the various commanders. So I would offer that into evidence on my oral representations, which is the way I know we've been offering these sort of collections that have come from that search warrant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, there's a major objection on that one. First of all, the fact that that document lists the names of the commanders, some of which were said, doesn't mean that what's contained in the rest of the document is true, accurate, and complete. So they can't go through the front door. Now we're trying to get through the keyhole or the back door. There's absolutely no foundation, no foundation. But they already read into the record the names of the commanders. It's widely known that this was a brigade that was going through commanders, you know, more or less every six months or what have you. So I don't think that's a problem. But we do have some major problems in allowing this document to come in unless a proper foundation can be laid. This is not just hearsay. It's hearsay upon hearsay upon hearsay. So we need to have some better foundation. They have another 11 weeks ahead of them to -- perhaps through some other witnesses, I don't know. They can certainly track down the author of this particular document. But this is like finding some kind of a document anywhere and because of what it says on top of it we give it some credence and weight. I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for the foundation of this document at this moment after hearing the explanations by the Prosecution, we have no doubt about it. As for the other part of the contents of this document, there may be some problems but we don't have the time to race through this document at this stage. So we'll not make a decision on whether we'll admit it into the evidence or not at this stage, but I hope in the meantime the Defence, since you challenge the admission, might furnish us with more details or reasons on your objections to that particular document so that to help us to arrive at the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So if I get the -- if I understand the Court correctly, the Court is saying that the Prosecution has laid a proper foundation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And might I ask, just for the record, for clarity, how was that foundation laid, Your Honour, other than the fact that they found it? Because now they're trying to get this entire document and the contents of the document for you to consider and give weight. And I just fail to see how, based on asking this gentleman a few questions. Are these the right commanders? And I knew exactly what they were doing because it's been done in other cases. It's not proper evidence, Your Honour. I'm afraid --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think we've already made our decision that we will not admit this document into the evidence at this stage. And we'll give you the opportunity to challenge anything you have doubts in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're putting the burden on me now. I'm having to challenge every page. So now I have to decide on each and every page whether it's true, accurate, and complete. It's the other way around. They need to establish how accurate this document is. Just because they've managed to get this gentleman to say these are the commanders, the onus should not be on me now to substantiate or unsubstantiate the contents of the document. It should be the other way around. Now, if you're asking me to help the Prosecution, find the witness, to bring him in, I can do that. He is available to the Prosecution, has been available to the Prosecution, I've offered to help them out. But what you're asking me now is to go through each page and try to raise objections as to why each page the Court should not accept when the Prosecution has not laid any foundation as to how each page is true, accurate, and complete. And I don't mean to be disputatious, Your Honour, I truly don't. And I apologise if I'm raising my voice, perhaps I'm a little tired. But it really seems a little unfair to be putting the onus on me to do their work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, we believe that as for the scope and the contents the Prosecution used through this witness, we believe it's sufficient to have this document admitted into the evidence. But as for the other contents, we don't have the time to read it. If it is an important document and concerning with the functions of the Bratunac Brigade, I believe that in the future this document will be used again and again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Just so the record is clear, the Prosecution only made reference to one particular page. We don't have a problem with that page coming in. The Prosecution did not make reference to any other part of the document. And of concern -- given the Court's ruling, I may now have to bring in somebody who authored this document in order to go through it page by page by page, which might require us to go beyond the 11 week -- because I truly believe, Your Honour, if the Prosecution in their case in-chief -- this is something that Butler wrote. They found this document. It merely says Bratunac Brigade history; that's all it says. Anybody could author it. Just like the map that we will go through that says Zivanovic zone of responsibility. We will show exactly how worthless that document is. But just to say because it says this in one page, list the particular commanders, that we're going to hold the Defence responsible for disproving what's in the document, I dare say, Your Honour -- and again, I don't mean to be disputatious. I accept the Court's ruling -- well, I accept that the Court is making the ruling. I disagree with the ruling. And I truly don't want to leave today with there be any feelings that there's animosity or discontent, other than professional disagreement on the admissibility of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As I said before, as for that one page, as you said, listing the names of the commanders, there's no problem. We could admit it into the evidence. We didn't do it at this moment. We'll wait until the future witness. I think maybe in the 11 weeks this document will be used again and again. And later on, we'll see whether we admit it as a whole of the document into the evidence or not. Is that agreeable to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. That's fine. Again, I apologise for raising my voice a little bit and getting a little excited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to clarify a little bit of that, Mr. President. The commanders' names are not on one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a history. And it's really more of a propaganda piece like all armies have about the glorious history of the war. I'm certainly not offering it to be completely truthful. But I did want to give you the whole document so you can see the document and give whatever weight you want to give it. But, you're right, there may be other issues that are related to it. But there's nothing underhanded going on here. We're just offering the document because this issue has been brought up repeatedly by the Defence about commanders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. I wish you have a pleasant journey back home after this session. The usher will show you out of the room. Thank you very much. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.
